The sum is p^(n-1)(3p-1)/2, but this rests on a recalled result and a guess for one of the three orders, not on a derivation or a checked source.

Aut(G) is isomorphic to the unit group of Z/p^n, which is cyclic of order p^(n-1)(p-1). It therefore has exactly one subgroup for each divisor of that order.

I did not derive which three subgroups give an almost commutative Terwilliger algebra. I recalled the result as follows:

- H = Aut(G), of order p^(n-1)(p-1).
- H of index 2 in Aut(G), of order p^(n-1)(p-1)/2.
- H the Sylow p-subgroup of Aut(G), of order p^(n-1). This third case is the part I am least sure of.

The sum of these orders is

p^(n-1)(p-1) + p^(n-1)(p-1)/2 + p^(n-1) = p^(n-1)(3p-1)/2.

ANSWER: $\frac{p^{n-1}(3p-1)}{2}$
